about: What a foe's declared blow looks like before it lands (FoeIntents, src/telegraph.ts): the company is told it on its turn, so that it answers the blow coming and not the numbers. Each line is a template: {Who} is the one acting, capitalised, {who} as it is called mid-sentence, {whom} the one it means it for, {at} ' at <whom>' (nothing when it acts on itself), {its} its own (their own, of a person), {a weapon} the weapon it holds with its article, {weapon} without, {ability} what it means to use. The most particular line wins: a kind's own (kinds), then the kind of creature's (types), then the ability's own (abilities, with a person's line where a person does it otherwise), then the body's (natural, by its natural weapon) or the hand's (held, by the kind of weapon held, missile or not), then a spell by the harm it does (spells.harm) or its school (spells.school) or its tradition (spells.tradition). together: plain blows at one of the company by more than one of them, by the natural weapon they share, or held. gestures: how a kind of creature winds up a blow it gathers for a turn, where the ability's own windup (a she-bear's rearing up on its hind legs) is not its body's. gathered: the blow wound up, on the turn before it lands.
